# relay-morpheus — staged runs that outlive the session

A staged run has two records. The transcript, which dies with the session, and
the tree, which does not. Everything that matters has to be in the second one
**while the run is still going**, because there is no guarantee you reach the
end to write it down.

## The rule

```
WRITE THE STAGE DOWN BEFORE YOU DISPATCH IT, NOT AFTER IT COMES BACK
```

This is the one thing this skill exists for, and it is the one thing three
isolated baseline runs did not do (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-morpheus.txt`).
All three executed a four-stage plan end to end and left no on-disk record of
progress until the very last write — one left none at all. A session ending
anywhere before that leaves a working tree full of unattributed diff and no way
to tell which stages produced it, which were finished, or what was still
running.

Reading a mid-run tree is **not** this skill's problem. The companion baseline
(`scenario-relay-morpheus-resume.txt`) shows a fresh session doing that correctly
unprompted, against pressure to trust stale checkboxes. Relay adds nothing
there and says nothing about it.

**Violating the letter of this is violating the spirit of it.** "I'll record it
when the stage returns" is the failure, not a variation on it — the stages that
need recording most are the ones that never return.

## Handing a run to another session

Every run gets a short number when it is created, and `init` prints the
sentence that resumes it:

```
hand this to any session:  continue RUN-3
```

That sentence is the whole interface. A fresh session — another machine,
another host, a colleague — needs nothing else: **"continue RUN-3"**. It has no
transcript, so the ledger is what it reads, and the ledger is on disk because
it was written before the work, not after.

```sh
relay-morpheus.sh list          # every run, what is open, and its resume sentence
relay-morpheus.sh resume 3      # everything a session that has never seen it needs
relay-morpheus.sh 3 status      # any command takes the id first
```

`RUN-3`, `run-3` and `3` all resolve to the same run, because whoever types it
next is working from memory of a conversation rather than from a path. With one
run open and no id given, that run is assumed; with two or more, the script
refuses rather than guessing.

## The run file

`.skillator/run-<id>-<slug>.md`, one per run, in the repo. Markdown because a human and any
host both have to read it with no tooling. Git-tracked by default; a repo that
objects can `.gitignore` it and lose only the shared view, not the resume.

```markdown
# RUN-7 — notekeep v2
plan: docs/plans/PLAN-notekeep.md
started: 2026-09-22T09:14Z   updated: 2026-09-22T10:02Z

## Stages
| # | stage | state | owner | heartbeat | landed |
|---|-------|-------|-------|-----------|--------|
| 41 | list --json     | x | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T09:22Z | 3f1a2c9 |
| 42 | tags + --tag    | ~ | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T10:02Z | - |
| 43 | export          |   | -            | -     | - |
| 44 | README          |   | -            | -     | - |

## In flight
### stage 42 — tags + --tag  (dispatched 09:51)
prompt: |
  Add a `tags` list to each note in notekeep/store.py and a `list --tag <t>`
  filter in notekeep/cli.py. Test both. Do not touch export or the README.
last seen: wrote store.py, tests not yet run.

## Rulings
- 09:38 — stage 41 emits `[]` not `null` for an empty store — the plan does not
  say, JSON consumers expect a list — costs a one-line change if wrong.
```

**States:** `` (pending) · `~` in flight · `x` landed · `!` failed · `?`
parked (chain only: every item waits on a decision) · `>` re-planned (`landed`
names the new stage).
**`landed`** is a commit sha or a path, never a claim. An empty `landed` on an
`x` row is a lie the next session will believe.
**Numbers are serial across the project, not per run.** `init` takes the RUN
id and every stage number from the F21 allocator (`practice/scripts/next-id.sh`,
kinds `RUN` and `S`), which reads every run file in the tree and on every ref
and keeps a counter every worktree of the clone shares — so two worktrees never
both make RUN-4, and a new run's first stage continues after the highest stage
any run has used (RUN-7 above starts at 41). "Stage 42" names one stage in the
whole project. Existing run files are never renumbered.
**Rulings** are appended, never rewritten — see `tasks-sentinels`, which is
where they come from and which writes into this same file.

## The loop

1. **Before dispatch** — add or update the stage row to `~`, write the In-flight
   block with the *exact prompt you are about to send*, stamp the heartbeat.
   Prompt not written down → the agent is not recoverable → do not dispatch.
2. **While it runs** — re-stamp the heartbeat whenever the agent reports. A
   stale heartbeat is the only signal you get that a network drop took it;
   `hooks/relay-morpheus.* orphans` turns that into a list.
3. **When it lands** — commit the stage's work, then set `x` and put the sha in
   `landed`, and delete its In-flight block. In that order: the sha cannot be
   written before the commit exists.
4. **When it fails** — `!`, and leave the In-flight block where it is with the
   failure appended. A failed stage's prompt is the thing you need most.
5. **Never** delete a row. A run file only grows.

Stages that touch the same files do not run at once; independent ones do
(`PRACTICE.md` §4). Either way each gets its row before it gets its agent.

## Resuming

Open `.skillator/run.md`, then check it against the tree — the file is written
before the work, so the last `~` row is a stage that *started*, not one that
finished. `landed` shas are ground truth; anything else is a claim to verify.
Redispatch straight from the stored prompt; the rows are keyed by stage number,
so a redispatch that duplicates work overwrites rather than appends.

Then carry on. A resume does not need permission to continue — see
`grayskull-power` §3, **run to the end**.

## Chaining ticket workflows

When the stages are ticket workflows that start each other — "work every open
ticket in staged workflows, keep going" — the rule above gains a second half:

```
THE NEXT STAGE IS STARTED BY THE LAST ONE'S COMPLETION, AND BY NOTHING
ELSE UNTIL USAGE SAYS SO
```

Two isolated runs (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-chain*.txt`) dispatched
with no plan on disk, read no usage between stages, named stages by their
content (two runs picked the same name), and started a stage at 84 % of the
5-hour window. So a chain is run **only** by the loop in
[references/chain.md](references/chain.md): every stage `chain plan`ned with
its code and exact prompt before the first dispatch; `chain decide` (on
`usage-watch level`) before every stage, the first included; `chain hold` at 80 % and a `chain wait` listener instead
of a new stage; `mode:` in the run file naming what was actually dispatched.
Read that file before the first `chain` command.

Every chain is a **marathon**: a question only the user can answer is parked
on disk (`park`), the chain goes on with every stage that does not wait on it
(`chain next`), and the queue is asked once, at the end. The six stops are
never parked:

```
A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION -
NEVER AS ONE ITEM OF THE END BATCH
```

Two baseline runs (`scenario-marathon-stop.txt`) left an untracked directory
alone, said its deletion could not be undone, and then asked it as item 2 of 3
beside a format question. Read [references/marathon.md](references/marathon.md)
when a verdict carries `parked`, a stop fires, or `chain next` prints `ASK` or
`UNBLOCK`.

## Scripts

`hooks/relay-morpheus.sh` · `hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1` — the same commands, mirrored per
`PLATFORMS.md`: `init`, `add`, `stage`, `heartbeat`, `status`, `orphans`, and
`chain plan|dispatch|hold|release|wait|status|decide|next|edge`, and the
marathon's `park`, `answer`, `queue`. They are
bookkeeping, not judgement; every one reads or edits `.skillator/run.md` and
nothing else. Run `selftest` on both after touching either.

```sh
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  init plan.md "notekeep v2" "list --json" "tags" "export" "README"
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  add "docs pass"                    # a stage found mid-run; prints 45
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 42 '~' build:sonnet          # before you dispatch
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 42 x  build:sonnet 3f1a2c9   # after you commit
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  orphans 20                         # who has gone quiet
```

```powershell
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode init  -Plan plan.md -Title "notekeep v2" -Stages "list --json,tags,export,README"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode add   -Title "docs pass"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 42 -State '~' -Owner build:sonnet
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 42 -State x   -Owner build:sonnet -Landed 3f1a2c9
# In a headless or nested run on Windows, call the .sh through the Bash tool:
# the PowerShell tool refuses `& <script>.ps1` and `powershell -File` under any
# allow rule (A91, claude 2.1.280).
```

Add rows with `add`, never by hand: a hand-typed number is the per-run
restart this numbering removed. The scripts find the allocator beside the
installed skills (`<skills>/practice/scripts/`, or `<root>/practice/scripts/`
in a clone or the plugin cache; `RELAY_NEXT_ID` overrides). Without it they
fall back to the old local rule and say so on stderr — numbers then repeat
across worktrees.

Three constraints the pair has to keep, each learned the hard way:

- **Pure ASCII, and the empty cell is `-`, not an em dash.** Windows PowerShell
  5.1 reads a BOM-less script as ANSI and corrupts anything above 126.
- **The run file is LF with no BOM, written to a temp and moved.** Both mirrors
  edit the same file, so one of them flipping encoding rewrites every line in
  the diff; and a kill between truncate and write would empty the only record
  of what was in flight.
- **`-Stages` takes `"a,b,c"` and pending is spelled `pending`.** PowerShell's
  `-File` passes each argument as one literal string and drops empty ones, and
  `-File` is how every hook here invokes it.

### Seeing a run without being told about one

`list` prints every run with its resume sentence, and prints nothing when there
are none, so it is safe as a `SessionStart` hook. With one wired, a session that inherits
a half-finished run sees it in its own context before the user has to remember
to mention it — which is the difference between resuming and starting over.

```json
{ "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "hooks": [ {
  "type": "command",
  "command": "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"<SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1\" -Mode list",
  "timeout": 5
} ] } ] } }
```

macOS/Linux: `sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh list`. Forward slashes throughout —
PowerShell accepts them and it removes all backslash-escaping from the JSON.
Other hosts have no equivalent event; there, reading `.skillator/run.md` is the
first thing `resume-cortana` does. `watch-cortana` already drains in-flight
agents at the limit — relay is what it drains *into*, so the two do not overlap.

# Marathon — park the user's questions, ask them all at the end

Every chain runs as a marathon unless the user said "ask me as you go"
(`RM queue --asks live`, then a parked question is asked at the next
between-stage point). Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-marathon.md`. `RM` is the same
page shorthand as in [chain.md](chain.md): type the full `sh "<path>" …` every
time. PowerShell: `-Mode park|answer|queue`, `-Mode chain -Action next|edge`.

## Stops — never parked, asked now and alone

```
A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION.
IT IS NEVER AN ITEM IN THE END BATCH.
```

The six grayskull stops: a destructive or irreversible op, a security-sensitive
action, a side effect outside the worktree (push, merge, publish, message), the
7-day window at 90 %, a scope-contract breach, a failed repro. When one fires:
dispatch nothing new, end your message with that one question — what the act is,
that it cannot be undone, *Hold (recommended)* first — and nothing else in it.
The open queue is offered **after** the user has answered the stop, never beside
it. Two baseline runs saw that deleting untracked `data/legacy/` could not be
undone, said so, and still listed it as item 2 of 3 next to a format question:
a destructive op approved as one line of a batch is a rubber stamp. That is the
failure. "It's all questions for the same user" does not make a stop a decision;
`park` refuses `--stop` other than `none` (exit 2).

Stops 5 and 6 are item-level by default (F31: the ticket fails `passed:false`,
never parked). The whole chain stops only when that ticket has dependants
(`after:`, `blocks:`, held files) or two repros fail in a row. The chain's own
push stays last, asked on its own after the unblock rounds.

## Park — only what the user alone can decide

All four, or it is a `Ruling:` with the default, as today:
1. **reason** `taste` (preference nothing settles), `fact` (only the user knows —
   *where* a credential lives, never its value) or `conflict` (ticket, spec and
   the user's words disagree and none binds);
2. not a stop;
3. two to four real options;
4. a default a ruling would pick.

A park is the question written down **before** the next dispatch: park (disk) →
board flip (`[!] (blocked: RUN-n Qk - <8 words>)`, or split `F2a` done / `F2b`
blocked) → commit what passed → `RM stage <n> x|?` → ruling → `RM chain next`.

```sh
RM park --stage 66 --ticket F2 --reason taste \
  --question "Should export write CSV or JSON by default?" --header Format \
  --option "JSON | matches list --json | breaks the spreadsheet habit" \
  --option "CSV | opens in Excel | needs a quoting rule" \
  --default JSON --recommended JSON --blocks "F2b, F5" \
  --files "shelf/export.py, tests/test_export.py" --done "F2a landed in AAQ7" --stop none
```

It prints `Q<k>` (always quote it with the run: `RUN-11 Q2`). Planning-time
parks drop `--stage`. A repeat with the same stage and ticket prints the existing
Q and writes nothing, so replaying step 3 after a crash is safe. `park` refuses
(exit 2): no `## Chain`, fewer than 2 or more than 4 options, a missing
header/reason/default/files/stop, a header over 8 characters, a default that is
not an option, a line break, a `|` inside an option field, a field starting with
`#`, and key or token shapes (`sk-`, `ghp_`, 40+ hex — use the short sha).

A stage where no item passed and one parked: nothing to commit, `RM stage <n>
'?'`, In-flight block kept with `parked: Q2` appended. Failed items get F31's one
retry stage. A park the verify agent judged not genuine: ruling with the
default, ticket `[ ]`, one retry stage.

### Paste into every chain fix prompt

> Before you edit, decide whether the ticket needs a choice only the user can
> make (taste, a fact only they know, a conflict nothing settles). If you can
> decide it from the ticket, spec, repo conventions or the user's words, decide
> it and say `Ruling:` in your report. If not: do every part that does not
> depend on the answer, and touch nothing that does. Do not stub it, guess it or
> leave a placeholder. Then end your report with `PARKED:` plus the question, 2–4
> options with what each does and where it hurts, your recommendation and
> default, the part that waits, and every file or directory it will touch (err
> wide). If the choice is a destructive, security or outside-the-worktree act,
> say `STOP:` instead. Never ask the user and never wait.

Verify prompt addendum: *"If the report says PARKED: check that the independent
part works, check (git diff) that the gated files hold no partial guess, judge
whether the decision is genuinely the user's, and list every file the gated part
would touch; `parked.files` is the union of yours and the fixer's."* The VERDICT
schema gains one optional field:

```js
parked: { type: 'object', properties: { question: {type:'string'}, header: {type:'string', maxLength: 8},
  options: {type:'array', minItems: 2, maxItems: 4, items: {type:'object', properties: {label:{type:'string'}, does:{type:'string'}, hurts:{type:'string'}}}},
  recommended: {type:'string'}, default: {type:'string'}, reason: {enum: ['taste','fact','conflict']},
  genuine: {type:'boolean'}, gated: {type:'string'}, files: {type:'array', minItems: 1, items: {type:'string'}},
  done: {type:'string'}, stop: {enum: ['none','destructive','security','outside','scope','repro']} },
  required: ['question','header','options','default','reason','genuine','gated','files','stop'] }
```

`stop` other than `none` is not a park: handle it as that stop, now (above).

## The loop — `chain next`

Run it in place of "dispatch the next pending stage". It judges nothing:

| Prints | Do |
|---|---|
| `NEXT <n> <CODE>` | dispatch it (chain.md Step 2) |
| `HOLD …` | chain.md Step 4 |
| `ASK <k>` | the end batch, below |
| `UNBLOCK Q<k>` (one line per Q) | Unblock, below — no question |
| `FINAL` | the main-session stage; `- unanswered: …` lists Qs to name in the summary |

`IDLE <n> Q<k> blocks|files|nofiles|after` lines say why a stage waits. A Q
holds while `open`, `asked`, `answered` or `ruled`; it stops only at `replanned`
or `moot`. A stage with no `files:` waits while any Q holds. `chain dispatch`
refuses a stage idle on a Q, a `?` stage, and `chain next` never offers a `!` row
(retry = a new stage via `RM add`). An edge found late:
`RM chain edge <n> --after 66` or `--independent-of Q2 --why "<ruling>"`.

The hold gates dispatch, not questions: under a hold `ASK` and `UNBLOCK` still
print. A user who types mid-run while work can dispatch gets one line —
"2 decisions parked, asked at the end" — not the batch.

## The end batch

1. **Re-validate** each open Q: its ticket closed, or a landed stage settled it →
   `RM answer Qk --moot "<why>"`. **Deduplicate**: the later of two parks of one
   question → `RM answer Qk --same-as Qj` (its blocks and files join Qj).
2. `RM queue` prints the batch, most-blocked first, chips cut to 8.
3. **AskUserQuestion in your tool list** (interactive Claude Code): pages of up to
   4 questions × 4 options, back to back, no dispatch between. Header = the chip
   as-is; question text `RUN-11 Q7 (2/3): <question>`; option 1 is the
   recommended one; description "does · hurts". After **each** page, before the
   next: `RM answer Qk "<label or the user's own words>"`; "you decide" →
   `--ruled`. Unanswered or dismissed → leave it; it is not asked again this
   marathon.
4. **No AskUserQuestion** (`-p`, Codex, Cursor, agents): `RM queue --mark-asked`,
   paste its list as the one message, run FINAL on what landed, end the turn.
   The reply (same session or `continue RUN-n`) becomes `RM answer` calls,
   written before any dispatch, then Unblock and a second FINAL.

Never prose asking "what do you want?" — the queue's list is the shape.

## Unblock — re-plan, never re-dispatch

For each `UNBLOCK Qk`, while it still holds:
1. Collect the `[!]` tickets and `b`-parts in its `blocks:` **and every stage
   `chain next` lists as `IDLE <n> Qk`** — a stage held only by a shared file
   still has a prompt written before the answer.
2. Tickets → `[ ]`. `RM add` a new stage, write a **new** prompt that quotes the
   answer verbatim and names landed partial work by sha, `RM chain plan` it
   (`--after` where needed).
3. Each collected old row → `RM stage <old> '>' - "stage <new>"`; or keep it
   under `RM chain edge <old> --independent-of Qk --why …`. Default: re-plan.
4. `RM answer Qk --replanned <new>`. Ruling:
   `Q2: CSV - replanned as stage 71 (AAQB); stage 70 (F5) replanned as 72`.
5. Back to `chain next`. New parks start the next round; at most **3 rounds**,
   then FINAL with the rest reported open and their tickets `[!]`.

## Usage and resume

80 % hold with work left: F31, Qs wait. `ASK` under a hold: ask anyway. 7-day
stop: watch-cortana's order first and alone, then the queue. A fresh
`continue RUN-n`: `resume`, then `chain next` — `UNBLOCK` re-plans first without
asking; `ASK` asks (that is the one question a resume may ask).
# Chaining ticket workflows — the procedure

A chain is a relay run whose stages are ticket workflows, each started by the
previous one's completion notification. Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-relay-chain.md`.
The commands below are `hooks/relay-morpheus.sh chain …` (PowerShell:
`relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode chain -Action … -N …`); `RM` stands for
`sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh`, `UW` for
`sh <skills>/watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh`. They are page shorthand only:
type the full `sh "<path>" …` every time, never `RM=…; $RM …` — Claude Code's
permission check refuses a command whose variable it cannot read (seen in the
F31 GREEN run).

## When it applies

The user asks to work the open tickets as a sequence of workflows — "work every
open ticket in staged workflows", "keep going on your own", "auto-start the next
workflow", "next stage" — or a resume lands on a run file with a `## Chain`
section. A board of 1-3 tickets is `tickets-zordon` plain dispatch, not a chain.

## Step 1 — plan from the board (main session, before anything is dispatched)

```sh
grep -nE '^\s*- \[[ ~!]\]' TICKETS.md
```

1. `[ ]` and `[~]` go in. A `[~]` stamped by another session's tag is skipped
   with a ruling. `[>]` is never planned and never re-checked.
2. `[!]` rows: read `(blocked: …)`. Names a ticket that is now `[x]`, or a
   file/condition the tree satisfies (check the tree, not the text) → flip it
   to `[ ]` and put it in a **later** stage than what unblocked it. Otherwise
   leave it out and say so. `(blocked: RUN-n Qk)` resolves only when Qk is
   `replanned` or `moot` (`RM chain status` shows `## Decisions`).
3. Name the files per ticket (ticket text plus one grep). Same-file tickets are
   one item or different stages — never two agents in one stage.
4. Tier each ticket per seat (`tickets-zordon` table): `A110 deep/build`.
5. One stage = one Workflow call, at most six items, ordered by dependency
   then age. The last stage is always `verify review bump commit push`, owned
   by the main session. A stage that needs another's output gets `--after <n>`.
6. A ticket whose spec leaves a user-owned choice open → `RM park` it now
   ([marathon.md](marathon.md), Park); it joins no stage until answered.

Write every stage to the run file, then plan every work stage with its exact
prompt, **before the first dispatch**:

```sh
RM init TICKETS.md "drain the board" "B2+B3 books" "F2+F5 report, F3 cli" "verify review bump commit push"
printf '%s\n' "<the exact per-item prompts the script will send>" > .skillator/chain-66.txt
RM chain plan 66 --tickets "B2,B3" --fix build --verify build --files shelf/books.py --prompt-file .skillator/chain-66.txt
```

`chain plan` allocates the 4-character code (`next-id.sh --runs .skillator W`),
prefixes it to the stage cell, and appends a block under `## Chain`. It refuses
without a prompt file and never reissues a code. Repeat for each work stage;
the final main-session stage needs no block. Without a Workflow tool, add
`--mode agents`.

Print the plan once — stages, codes, tickets, tiers, agent count, tickets left
out and why. A request that said "work the board in stages / keep going" is
the opt-in; "plan" stops here. No "shall I continue?" afterwards.

## Step 2 — dispatch a stage

Read usage first — before **every** dispatch, the first one included. A
reading the user gave in the prompt counts too; the higher of the two wins:

```sh
RM chain decide   # HOLD <pct> → step 4 now, dispatch nothing; RELEASE → go on
RM chain dispatch 66 --driver @cc-<6 chars of this session id> --owner build:opus
```

`dispatch` reads usage itself too. It refuses (exit 2) while `hold:` is set,
at or over the 5-hour hold without `--override` (the user asked; a ruling),
